title: The Universe You Can't See: Part 1
hook: Part one: fresh bananas emit real nuclear radiation into your home.
script: Part one: fresh bananas emit real nuclear radiation into your home. What would actually happen if you ate a million at once? One banana gives about 0.1 microsieverts of exposure from potassium-40. Massive cargo crates of them regularly trigger nuclear sensors at border checkpoints. Yet radiation is not what harms you. Plain potassium stops your heart first. Your own body fires potassium-40 decays roughly 5,000 times a second. Your kidneys flush the excess, so that internal dose never adds up. Does sharing a bed with a radiating human comfort or unsettle you? Follow so you do not miss part two.

captions: The Universe You Can't See (Part 1): Banana radiation is real, but you radiate far more. Comforting or creepy?
Every eight hours in bed with another person exposes you to half a banana of gamma radiation. Would you sleep alone instead?
Your kidneys flush extra potassium so fast that banana dose never accumulates. Did you expect your own body to be more radioactive than your food?
